'''Nazzar''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] bipedal [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Nazzri]]. With [[Equine/Legends|equine]] faces and powerfully built bodies, the species had a history of contemplation and philosophy. They were mildly xenophobic, and were rarely found off their temperate [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]; the only offworld Nazzar were outcasts. One of the most famous Nazzar was the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Qrrrl Toq]], who fought and [[Death/Legends|died]] in the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], around [[4000 BBY/Legends|four thousand years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].

Noble and spiritual people, the Nazzar joined the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] early in its history. They followed the ''[[Ulizra]]'', a strict Nazzar religion, which stated that outsiders were likely to taint Nazzar culture, and that the group was always better than the individual.

==Biology and appearance==
Averaging roughly two [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall, Nazzar were bipedal, [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]], with distinctly elongated [[Equine/Legends|equine]] heads, and were known to have been a physically powerful and agile [[Species/Legends|species]]. Likewise, Nazzar had dark skin covered with a thin coat of [[Hair/Legends|fur]], which usually ranged in color from light gray to dark navy. The species were distinguished by two long [[Ear/Legends|ears]] that lay limp at the sides of their heads, and strong, four-fingered [[Limb/Legends|hands]].<ref name="UAA" /> A common piece of a Nazzar regalia was a harness-like set of straps worn around the muzzle.<ref>See ''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]'', ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'', and [[Knights of the Old Republic 43|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 43]], for example.</ref>

Nazzar had an average lifespan slightly longer than those of most sentient species in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Considered [[Youngling/Legends|younglings]] until they were eleven standard years old, Nazzar became adults when they reached eighteen. At around fifty-six [[Standard year/Legends|years]], Nazzar were regarded as middle-aged, while those who reached ninety were thought of as old. Anyone older than one hundred twenty-five years was considered venerable, and demanded much respect from society.<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==
Nazzar were deeply spiritual and distant, and extremely intolerant of other forms of religion and belief, especially those dissimilar to their own. The offworld Nazzar who eventually overcame their xenophobia and natural prejudice formed friendships with many other species in the galaxy, and were said to make trusted and loyal companions.<ref name="UAA" />

[[File:Qrrl_Toq_TOTJC.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Nazzar male.]]
Nazzar followed a state religion, which was known as ''Ulizra'', and the Nazzar government expected strict adherence to the tenets of the fourteen sects,<ref name="UAA" /> each ruled by a [[Prefect/Legends|praefect]] of the religion. Those tenets included the concepts that outsiders would contaminate and taint Nazzar society and culture; that Nazzar individuals should remain in seclusion from the rest of the galaxy;<ref name="TOTJC">''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]''</ref> that all philosophical systems were in disagreement with ''Ulizra''; and that the group was always more important than the individual. Because of these beliefs, it was very difficult for other species to set up trade relations with the Nazzar, or even for Nazzar to befriend those of another species. Although legally allowed, outsiders who stayed on Nazzri usually received a less than warm welcome.<ref name="UAA" />

Spread over three [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], the Nazzar government had originally formed as a [[King/Legends|monarchy]], but over many millennia it became an [[Oligarchy|oligarchical]] [[theocracy]] led by a king and fourteen praefects, the heads of each of the sects of the Nazzar religion. The king presided over the council of fifteen lawgivers and commanded the Nazzri military forces and planetary security agencies. However, only the praefects could introduce and vote on new laws and amendments. A majority of the Nazzar could correctly predict almost any vote, as the praefacts could not break any of the tenets of ''Ulizra'' in their decisions.<ref name="TOTJC" />

Nazzar spoke a [[Nazzar (language)|language of the same name]], as well as [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]]. Examples of Nazzar names included "Brryg Tallak," "Drrn Roqar," "Srrn Kanas," and "Vrrk Jikat."<ref name="UAA" />

==History==
The [[Nazzri system/Legends|Nazzri system]] joined the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] early in [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|galactic history]],<ref name="UAA" /> becoming part of the [[Lantillian sector/Legends|Lantillian sector]] and located on a large [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]],<ref name="Inner Rim Extra">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> but had little contact with the Republic apart from maintaining a [[Galactic Senate/Legends|senatorial]] presence on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. When [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] rose to power, most Nazzar returned to their system and ignored the going-ons in the galaxy. That attitude continued into the time of the [[New Jedi Order]], and despite several invitations, Nazzri did not join the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. The Nazzar also ignored the events of the galaxy around them during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="UAA" />

An entire history of the Nazzar race was housed within the [[Hall of Edification]], an ancient building on their homeworld.<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

==Nazzar in the galaxy==
[[File:Qrrrltoq.jpg|thumb|210px|The Nazzar Jedi Qrrrl Toq.]]
Due to their somewhat xenophobic nature, Nazzar were rarely seen away from their home planet; a temperate and lushly vegetated world known as Nazzri, which was located in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] region of the galaxy. Offworld Nazzar were likely to be either outcasts who had denounced and rejected the teachings and ideas of ''Ulizra'' or preachers who had left their planet to attempt to bring their philosophical truths to new people; however, Nazzar preachers rarely found acceptance of Ulizra offworld, and many returned home. Nazzar outcasts managed to find new organizations to follow, and many became fanatical followers of a wide range of fringe groups.<ref name="UAA" />

Although extremely rare, Nazzar who had proved themselves as devout followers of ''Ulizra'' were permitted to leave the planet on a self-imposed exile known as a ''[[boqeri]]'', on which Nazzar sought spiritual truth. The length of a ''boqeri'' depended on how long it took the seeker to discover the truth they did not know at home. Records indicated that there were several Nazzar on those journeys were fascinated by the wonders of the galaxy and never returned to Nazzri. Many of them were drawn to adventure; Nazzri soldiers, [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] and [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were not uncommon prior to the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="UAA" />

[[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Qrrrl Toq]] was a notable member of the Nazzar race, and one who had ventured away from his homeworld to prosper in the wider galaxy. The son of the Nazzar emperor-king, he was trained in the ways of the ''Ulizra'' by fellow Nazzar [[Vrrk Jikat]]. Toq left his homeworld to perform his ''boqeri'', and on [[Ulda Frav]] he encountered a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] for the first time. The Jedi, realizing Toq was strong in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], took him to [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]] to be trained by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Vodo-Siosk Baas]].<ref name="TOTJC" /> Toq fought in the [[Freedon Nadd Uprising]]<ref name="FNU2">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising'' 2]]</ref> of [[3998 BBY]]<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> and the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], although he was killed when the [[Krath/Legends|Krath]] sorceress named [[Aleema Keto]] triggered a [[Cron Supernova/Legends|supernova]] of almost a dozen [[Star/Legends|stars]].<ref name="TSW4">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 4|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 4]]</ref>

[[Ikree]] was a Nazzar [[Prince/Legends|princess]] who, after returning from her ''boqeri'', discovered that her father, the emperor-king, was corrupted by dark magic. When her father refused to stop using the magic, she spoke out against the government. She was imprisoned, and later killed by one of her father's subordinates.<ref name="TOTJC" />

In [[3963 BBY]], a member of the Nazzar species named [[Qohn]] was owned as a [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] by the [[Sungrazer cooperative]], which used slaves in its dangerous [[Thorilide/Legends|thorilide]] harvesting operations. Qohn had outlived all other slaves owned by the group, so he acted as a sort of intermediary between his masters and fellow captives. When [[Jarael]] and [[Zayne Carrick]] arrived on the ship ''[[Sungrazer]]'', where Qohn was kept, they staged an attempted rescue of Qohn and the other slaves during a thorlide dive. However, the mining ship [[Gladiator (Crucible)|''Gladiator'']] arrived and stymied the plan.<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic 43">[[Knights of the Old Republic 43|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 43]]</ref> In [[1032 BBY/Legends|1032 BBY]], a [[Unidentified Nazzar icecrawler driver|Nazzar]] served the [[Arkadianate]] on the planet [[Syned]] as an [[Icecrawler/Legends|icecrawler]] driver. As he drove a crawlerful of refugees from the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Diligence (New Sith Wars)|''Diligence'']] to the planet's [[City/Legends|capital]], [[Calimondretta]], the Nazzar fell victim to [[Jarrow Rusher]], the [[Captain/Legends|captain]] of the ''Diligence'', who led his crew in an attack on the Arkadianites to steal the vehicle for use in an [[Siege of Calimondretta|assault]] on Calimondretta.<ref name="KEn 23">[[Knight Errant (novel)|''Knight Errant'']], Chapter 23</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Nazzar were first created by authors [[Tom Veitch]] and [[Kevin J. Anderson]] for [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising|''The Freedon Nadd Uprising'']], which was part of the [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Tales of the Jedi'']] comic series. ''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]'', a [[West End Games]] ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' sourcebook, fleshed out their history, and, several years later, a [[Wizards of the Coast]] sourcebook, ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'', further expanded the species' culture and history.
